## {{< var planned >}} `check()` {#sec-check}

The `check()` function first reads and parses a `request.yaml` and a metadata
file, `datapackage.json`, checking that they contain the required keys. It then
runs the checks described below in order, returning a `CheckError` if any check
fails.

<!-- TODO: We could consider bundling up the errors and return a vector of CheckError's instead? -->

```{mermaid}

%%| fig-cap: "The flow of input and output through the check function."

%%|   The user provides the request and metadata file. The function completes a
%%|   set of checks, before returning a result that's either the unit type or a
%%|   CheckError.

    subgraph check ["check()"]

      read_metadata["read_metadata()<br>Parse metadata file into a Package struct"]
      check_package_name["check_package_name()<br>Package name matches metadata"]
      check_package_version["check_package_version()<br>Package version matches metadata"]
      check_resource_names["check_resource_names()<br>Resource names match metadata"]
      check_column_names["check_column_names()<br>Column names match metadata"]
      check_row_filters["check_row_filters()<br>Row filters match metadata columns"]
    end

    request --> read_request --> check_package_name --> check_package_version --> check_resource_names --> check_column_names --> check_row_filters --> output
```

```rs
/// Checks a request yaml against the metadata file.
///
/// The checks include:
///
/// - Required sections and keys are present in the request and metadata.
/// - Data package name and version in the request matches the metadata.
/// - The resources and columns in the request exist in the metadata.
/// - The row filters match columns in the metadata.
///
/// Errors if the request or metadata file can't be read, or if any
/// check fails.
pub fn check(request: Path, metadata: Path) -> Result<(), CheckError> {
    let request = read_request(request);
    let metadata = read_metadata(metadata);
    // Package name and version matches metadata.
    check_package_name(&request, &metadata);
    check_package_version(&request, &metadata);
    // Resource names match metadata.
    check_resource_names(&request, &metadata);
    // Column names match metadata.
    check_column_names(&request, &metadata);
    // Row filters match metadata columns (including whether the operator
    // types and values are allowed with the column type).
    check_row_filters(&request, &metadata);

    Ok(())
}
```

## {{< var planned >}} `subset_resources()`

`subset_resources()` takes the data package metadata and the request details and
applies the request to the resources into a data subset. While also visually
shown in the diagram below, briefly, it needs to:

1. Keep the selected resources.
2. Read in the resource data.
3. Row-filter the resources and keep the primary keys.
4. Combine all the kept resource primary keys.
5. Row-filter *all* the resources again on the keys.
6. Keep all the selected columns in the resources.
7. Output all the kept data, along with the resource's name (for later
   processing).

We need to filter all resources by the keys *after* the first row-filtering in
order to create the correct population for the research project.

The signature is:

```text
subset_resources(rap: Rap) -> Result<Arc<SubsettedResource>, Errors>
```

<!-- TODO: Arc for Ids may need to be Vec -->
